newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges U.S. caution on Taiwan president trip.
newsitem.headline: China urges U.S. caution on Taiwan president trip.

text.p: China called on Washington on Tuesday to ensure that Taiwan's President Lee Teng-hui would not conduct activities harmful to the unity of the motherland with his plans to transit the United States.

"We hope the American side ... will not allow key Taiwan political figures to create 'two Chinas' or 'one China, one Taiwan' or conduct activities to split the motherland under the name of transiting the country," Foreign Ministry spokesman Tang Guoqiang told reporters.
Taipei said on Monday it would ask Washington to grant Taiwanese President Lee a transit visa despite an expected protest from China, the island's arch rival.

The United States, which does not have official ties with Taiwan, said in April that Lee was eligible for a visa to transit the U.S. on his way to a September conference in Panama, one of about 30 nations that recognises the island.

Beijing, which views Taiwan as a rebel-ruled province and seeks to isolate its leaders from the international arena, was furious when Washington allowed Lee to visit his alma mater Cornell University in June 1995.
Beijing has also protested the many instances where Taiwan's vice-president, foreign minister and other high officials have been granted visas to visit or tranist the United States.
